task_instance: Create a new Expo (SDK 57) TypeScript app, install @expo/ui, and build a screen using the skill's documented universal components (Host, BottomSheet, Column, Text, Button, Switch) reproducing the skill's own BottomSheet example (a button that opens a native BottomSheet showing a cafe detail), then bundle/export it for the web platform (react-native-web/react-dom, one of the three platforms the universal layer targets) and verify the compiled output actually contains the component tree and its content.
evidence: In ExpoUIDemo/: `npx create-expo-app@latest ExpoUIDemo --template blank-typescript` (Expo SDK ~57.0.25, satisfies the skill's SDK 56+ requirement for the universal layer). `npm install` then `npm install @expo/ui@latest` (resolved @expo/ui 57.0.20; used plain npm because `npx expo install` failed with 'HTTP Proxy Network Error: Forbidden' when it tried to phone home for a compatibility check -- worked around with npm directly, which is allowed). Wrote App.tsx importing `Host, BottomSheet, Column, Text, Button, Switch` from `@expo/ui` and reproducing the skill's documented BottomSheet pattern (isPresented/onDismiss/snapPoints=['half','full']) plus a Switch, matching the skill's component table. Installed react-native-web, @expo/metro-runtime, and pinned react-dom@19.2.3 (peer requirement) with --legacy-peer-deps. Ran `EXPO_NO_TELEMETRY=1 EXPO_OFFLINE=1 EXPO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 npx expo export -p web`, which succeeded: 'Web Bundled 8393ms index.ts (301 modules)' producing dist/_expo/static/js/web/index-*.js (517KB) plus index.html/favicon/metadata.json. Verified the deliverable by grepping the compiled bundle: it contains 2 occurrences of 'BottomSheet' and the exact app strings 'Caf\xe9 details', 'Caf\xe9 Nocturne', 'Rue de la Paix', and 'Notifications', confirming the @expo/ui component tree (Host/BottomSheet/Column/Text/Button/Switch) was correctly resolved, transpiled and bundled with its content intact. Served dist/ via `python3 -m http.server` and confirmed index.html returned HTTP 200. Did not attempt an iOS/Android simulator build (no simulator/device tooling available in this text-only runtime); that goes beyond the universal layer's web-capable subset, which is what was exercised and verified here. No MCP/connector tools were used, per the safety rules.
